items.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: I worked with Bobby Hutcherson, mostly in the seventies, and we’d go to Europe a lot.

ctx.x: Did you ever have to do anything for living along the way besides playing drums?

Oh yes. But let me tell you, like okay. My wife, my present wife of 21 years now, had two children when we met. I had three. All boys. Five boys. And I’ll never forget — and most of the time I was on the road, that’s how I made my money. So as long as I was on the road all the time I could do okay. So I didn’t have any really ridiculous habits, I just sent my money home. And it worked out all right. items.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: I moved – Delano Dean, who used to live next to Jackie Robinson on Pepper Street, he had moved up here to San Francisco, and he opened up a club called the

Both/And. I always wondered, what was the meaning of that title? Both/And is out of the Bible: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost – Both/And. A lot of people don’t know that. So I came up here. Because of me living up here, it became increasingly hard for me and Harold to work, because him being in L.A., although we did do several albums. One was called San Francisco, which had a big funky hit on it, called Ummh. It became the theme song for when the Watts Jazz Festival was going on. I called George Butler.…
